transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Thanks for coming in today—what brings you in to see me?

Hey, Dr. Smith. Yeah, well... what finally got me here is that work is just getting really messed up. I'm an electrician, and lately I just can’t keep my focus on one estimate or code form anymore. 

Like, I'll sit down to do the paperwork, and then I hear a tool noise, or someone texts me... which actually reminds me, my buddy texted me this crazy article about how copper prices are supposed to spike again, and I was thinking I should probably go buy out the supply house of 12/2 wire before it happens. I mean, the markup we have to pass on to the customer is getting ridiculous, and people get so mad about it, like I control the global metal market, you know? I had this one lady last month who practically yelled at me over the cost of an outlet swap. 

But, uh... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the forms. Yeah, so a text comes in, or I hear a noise, or I get some huge new idea about redesigning the workshop, and it just pulls me completely off track. And then my jobs start getting mixed up. So... yeah, I guess that's why I'm here.
Over the past week or so, have you noticed needing much less sleep than usual while still feeling full of energy, or feeling unusually upbeat, confident, or 'on top of the world'?

Yeah, actually, sleep has been... well, I don't really need much lately. Honestly, for months now I’ve been getting maybe three or four hours a night? But I don't feel tired at all. I just pop right up before dawn, totally wired and ready to go. I'll start answering emails, pricing out materials, or sketching out whole new electrical systems like I just had a full night's rest. 

Like the other morning, it was maybe 3:30 AM, and I started sketching this massive smart-home integration for a client. Which is funny because they didn't even ask for it, but I figured, hey, future-proofing, right? And speaking of smart homes, it's wild how everything is on Wi-Fi now. My buddy Dave—he's a plumber—he was telling me they have these Wi-Fi enabled water heaters now. A water heater! Why do you need to text your water heater? I mean, I guess if you're on vacation and want to save a few bucks on gas, but Dave says the sensors break constantly. He had to drive out to this massive house in the hills last week just to reset a router for a boiler. Can you imagine paying a plumber's hourly rate for IT work? It's a total racket. Dave makes good money doing it, though, so I can't really blame him, and he just bought this new truck with the extra storage bed... 

But, uh... wait, did you ask about Dave? No, you asked about sleep. Yeah, so three or four hours is plenty for me right now. I feel great.
Have you ever had a period, lasting two weeks or more, where you felt persistently sad, low, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

Sad? No, not really. I mean, I don't get sad like that. I've always been a pretty upbeat guy, you know? Even when work is stressful or whatever. Actually, speaking of stressful, you wouldn't believe the supply chain issues we're having right now with breaker panels. It is a nightmare. I ordered a 200-amp panel for a residential upgrade like three weeks ago, and my rep at the supply house—this guy Mike, great guy, he used to play minor league baseball actually, pitched a few games in double-A before he blew out his shoulder. Such a shame, he had a killer slider. Anyway, Mike tells me they are backordered for another month. A month! How am I supposed to finish a rough-in if I don't have the panel? The general contractor is breathing down my neck, sending me these passive-aggressive emails at like 9 PM. Like, buddy, I can't manufacture a Siemens panel in my garage, okay? Though honestly, with the way things are going, I should probably start looking into 3D printing components or something. I saw this video on YouTube where a guy 3D printed a whole functioning gear box. It's crazy what they can do now with those resin printers. You have to be careful with the fumes, though, they're super toxic. 

But yeah, anyway... what were we talking about? Oh, being sad. No, I haven't really felt low or anything like that. Just been going, going, going.
Have you ever had a period like this before—either with this same kind of high energy and reduced sleep, or a distinct period of depression—at any other time in your life, even years ago?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've always been a hard worker, you know? Put my head down, get the job done. That's how my dad raised me. He was an electrician too, actually. He ran his own shop for like thirty years back in Chicago before he retired. Moved down to Florida, bought a boat. A pontoon boat, which I told him was a mistake because they're basically just floating patios, you can't really take them out if the water gets choppy. But he loves it. He goes out there with his buddies, they drink cheap beer and try to catch snapper. He was telling me last week about this massive storm that rolled in while they were out near the keys, and they had to haul ass back to the marina. The motor stalled on him twice. I keep telling him he needs to upgrade to a Yamaha outboard, those things are bulletproof, but he's stubborn. Typical old school tradesman, right? If it ain't completely broken, don't fix it. 

But, uh... what was the question? Oh, if I've been like this before. No, not really. Just been feeling really dialed in lately, you know?

Wait, what was the question? I think I lost my train of thought. We were talking about my dad's boat, right? Or wait, you asked something before that. Honestly, my mind is just racing a mile a minute today. I was actually thinking about the wiring on that boat, because salt water just eats through copper like you wouldn't believe. You have to use tinned marine-grade wire for everything, otherwise you're just asking for a short circuit. And don't even get me started on the battery terminals. My dad just slaps some grease on them and calls it a day, but I keep telling him he needs to use proper heat-shrink tubing. I brought some down last time I visited, this really nice dual-wall stuff with adhesive inside. Melts perfectly. We went to this seafood place afterwards, amazing crab legs, but the service was so slow... 

Anyway, I'm sorry, what were you asking me? I completely forgot.
Has this burst of energy and racing thoughts caused any real problems for you—like missed deadlines, impulsive spending, conflicts with coworkers or family, or anything you've later regretted?

Problems? Well, I mean... my wife and I have been arguing a lot lately. She says I'm putting everything we built at risk, with the business and the mortgage and all that. Which, you know, mortgages are a whole scam anyway if you think about it. The interest they charge you over thirty years, you end up paying for the house twice over. I was looking at our amortization schedule the other night at like 3 AM, and it's just robbery. I actually thought about just cashing out some of my tools to pay down the principal, but I need those. Like my Klein lineman pliers, you can't just replace those with some cheap knockoff from Home Depot. The steel isn't the same. I had a pair of Milwaukee ones once, and the cutting edge chipped on a piece of 12-gauge wire. Unbelievable. 

But yeah, my wife is stressed. And work... well, some clients have been complaining. Saying I missed details or mixed up the schedule. And my apprentices, they're looking at me funny, like they don't trust my direction anymore. Which is ridiculous because I've forgotten more about electrical code than they'll ever know. I had to explain to my one guy, Tommy, three times last week how to properly bond a subpanel. Three times! He just stares at me with this blank look. Kids these days, they just want to look at their phones. Speaking of phones, my battery keeps dying so fast lately, I think the lithium-ion cell is degrading. I should probably order a replacement kit and swap it out myself, it's not that hard if you have the right suction cup tool for the screen... 

Wait, did that answer your question? About the problems?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a first-ever, distinct episode characterized by markedly decreased need for sleep (3-4 hours with no fatigue), subjective energy increase, flight of ideas/racing thoughts, marked distractibility, grandiosity (elaborate unsolicited project plans, overvaluing own expertise), irritability, and impulsive financial ideation (cashing out tools to pay mortgage). No hallucinations, delusions, or other psychotic features were elicited despite grandiose and tangential thinking, supporting 'without psychotic symptoms' rather than F30.2. The disorganized, distractible speech represents flight of ideas rather than formal thought disorder.
